intro: Security work builds coordination, judgment and the ability to stay calm with the public. Among the 25 careers below, the closest fit for former security guards is Correctional Officers and Jailers, with an 88% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $58,940, or 55% more than guards earn.
why_it_works: A guard watches for problems, writes clear reports and decides fast when something looks wrong. O*NET rates judgment and decision making at 3 out of 5 here, the same core that police, dispatch and parking enforcement jobs use. Many of these roles pay far more than the $38,020 guard median. Some need a police academy or certificate, and the skills to grow are time management and leading a team.
tips: Keep copies of incident reports you wrote; clear writing is tested in police and corrections hiring.
Check public safety dispatcher openings: telecommunicators earn $53,040, which is 40% more, with no extra degree.
Ask local agencies about academy sponsorship before paying for training yourself.

faq.q: What jobs can former security guards do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Correctional Officers and Jailers (88%), Transit and Railroad Police (86%) and Parking Enforcement Workers (86%), based on O*NET 31.0. Police and Sheriff's Patrol Officers follow at 85%, with a median of $76,210, which is 100% more than the $38,020 guard median.

faq.q: Which careers for former security guards pay more?
faq.a: 19 of the 25 matches pay more than security guards. Police and detective supervisors earn $106,040 (179% more), Transit and Railroad Police $90,230 (137% more) and railroad conductors $78,000 (105% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Supervisor roles usually require police experience first.

faq.q: Do security guards need a degree to switch careers?
faq.a: Not for most paths. 18 of the 25 matches need no more education than guards already have, and 92% of workers in the closest match have a high school diploma or the equivalent. Police roles usually require academy training or a certificate instead of a degree.

faq.q: What skills should security guards develop?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are social perceptiveness, time management, managing people and systems analysis. You already bring coordination, rated 3.12 out of 5 by O*NET, and persuasion at 2.88, which help in calming tense situations on any public safety job.
